method.selection_policy: LLM-selected market-relevant items from news_digest.json; preserves source metadata and excludes noise.

framework.Equities: Broad equity/risk sentiment; market-moving mega-cap/AI allowed; low-signal single-stock noise excluded.
framework.Commodities: Physical commodity futures framework; supply disruption/demand strength positive; supply increase/demand weakness negative.
framework.FX: USD-centric basket; non-USD currency strength positive; USD/DXY strength negative.
framework.Rates: Bond-price framework; yields up/selloff/higher-for-longer negative; yields down/bond rally/cooler inflation positive.

Equities.title: Equities: Tech slump contrasts broader resilience – Deutsche Bank
Equities.summary: Deutsche Bank’s Early Morning Reid describes a mixed picture for US equities. The S&P 500 index slipped 0.22% as chip stocks sold off sharply, yet the equal‑weighted S&P 500 rose 0.24% to a new record.
Equities.reason: Captures the dominant market narrative: sharp tech/chip weakness vs underlying breadth/resilience. Net negative risk impulse for growth/tech leadership but important cross-market nuance.

Equities.title: Chip stocks that notched record rallies in second quarter start Q3 with a dud
Equities.summary: Memory maker Micron, which jumped over 240% in the second quarter, dropped 11% on Wednesday, wiping out nearly $200 billion of market capitalization.
Equities.reason: Large-cap chip reversals are a high-signal hit to market leadership (AI/semis), increasing downside risk for growth indices and tech-centered flows.

Equities.title: South Korean Stocks Tumble 6% as AI Jitters Hurt Chipmakers
Equities.reason: Regional contagion from US tech/chip rout; a sharp, market-moving selloff that underscores systemic risk to global tech and EM/Asia equity flows.

Equities.title: Wall Street ends lower as tech shares slip
Equities.reason: US close lower driven by tech weakness and geopolitical concerns; reinforces negative near-term sentiment for equities.

Equities.title: Morning Bid: Shares pull back as markets await likely payrolls beat
Equities.reason: Macro risk event (US payrolls) driving cautious positioning; payrolls uncertainty amplifies short-term volatility across equity markets.

Equities.title: Tech Stocks Retreat Deepens Ahead of US Payrolls: Markets Wrap
Equities.reason: Reinforces the tech-led risk-off theme ahead of major macro data; meaningful for equity leadership rotation and intraday flows.

Equities.title: M&A Volume to Stay Strong in Second Half, Says Sullivan’s Sawyer
Equities.reason: Supporting narrative for equities: persistent M&A activity underpins corporate demand for equities and can prop up markets even amid sector rotation.

Equities.title: OpenAI proposes handing Trump administration 5% stake
Equities.summary: Sam Altman’s start-up in early talks for a public ownership deal as political pressure rises
Equities.reason: Policy/ownership move that could lower regulatory/political overhang for AI leaders — positive for AI/large-cap tech sentiment and risk appetite.

Equities.title: Russia launches massive strike on Ukraine as Poland scrambles jets, Finland restricts airspace
Equities.summary: The Russian defence ministry said that it launched a "massive strike using long-range precision air, land, and sea-based weapons and attack drones."
Equities.reason: Significant geopolitical escalation elevates risk-off dynamics and volatility, pressuring global equity markets and risk assets.

Equities.title: Japan Retail Investors Bought Record Stocks Last Week in Selloff
Equities.reason: Contrarian retail demand in a selloff provides modest support to markets; a lower-relevance, but useful, counter-signal to institutional outflows.

Rates.title: Switzerland’ CPI inflation meets expectation in June: What 0.5% means for Swiss Franc
Rates.summary: Switzerland’s Consumer Price Index (CPI) rose by 0.5% year-over-year (YoY) in June, compared to a rise of 0.6% in May, the latest data published by the Swiss Federal Statistical Office showed on Wednesday. The market consensus was for 0.5% growth in the report
Rates.reason: Slight deceleration in Swiss CPI (0.6%→0.5%) is mildly disinflationary, supportive for Swiss government bonds (yields lower). Market-moving for Swiss rates but domestically focused, so moderate relevance.

Rates.title: Euro bond yields tick up as hawkish Sintra rhetoric cools near-term cut hopes
Rates.reason: Direct report of euro-area bond yields rising as hawkish commentary reduces near-term cut expectations — clear negative for bond prices (yields up) with high relevance for core rates.

Rates.title: Nonfarm Payrolls set to show resilient US labor market, backing case for Fed rate hikes
Rates.summary: The United States (US) Bureau of Labor Statistics (BLS) will release the Nonfarm Payrolls (NFP) data for June on Thursday at 12:30 GMT.
Rates.reason: Expectations of resilient US NFP strengthen the case for further Fed hikes — negative for bond prices (yields higher). High relevance due to US rates and global policy transmission.

Rates.title: Foreign Traders Sell Biggest Pile of Japan Bonds in Three Years
Rates.reason: Large foreign selling of JGBs points to demand weakness and upward pressure on JGB yields — negative for Japanese bond prices and relevant for global rate dynamics.

Rates.title: Japan 10-Year Bond Sale Sees Weaker Demand Than 12-Month Average
Rates.reason: Weaker-than-normal demand at a benchmark JGB sale signals potential for higher JGB yields; meaningful for Japan rates but more localized, so moderate relevance.

Rates.title: Global Treasurers Fuel Record $36 Billion of Kangaroo Bond Sales
Rates.reason: Record issuance of kangaroo (AUD) bonds implies increased supply in global bond markets which can weigh on bond prices (upward pressure on yields); relevant to supply dynamics.

Rates.title: Can Kevin Warsh tame the Fed’s $7tn balance sheet?
Rates.summary: Pragmatism, not ideology, should be the guide
Rates.reason: Discussion of Fed balance-sheet runoff/management raises the prospect of reduced central-bank demand for Treasuries (structural supply pressure) — negative for bond prices with policy/market significance.

Rates.title: ECB to integrate non-financial credit claim portfolios into general collateral framework, phasing out temporary measures
Rates.reason: Operational change to ECB collateral and phasing out temporary measures normalises liquidity provision — modestly negative for bond prices if it reduces emergency liquidity/support.

Rates.title: Isabel Schnabel: Is inflation back?
Rates.reason: ECB commentary directly questioning a resurgence of inflation implies a hawkish tilt for policy and supports higher-for-longer yields — negative for bond prices with regional importance.

Rates.title: Japan’s Nagahama expects BoJ to raise interest rates again at the end of the year
Rates.summary: Toshihiro Nagahama, a key private-sector member on Japanese Prime Minister Takaichi's Council on Economic and Fiscal Policy, comments on the Bank of Japan’s (BoJ) monetary policy decision.
Rates.reason: Public expectation of another BoJ rate increase signals tighter JGB market and potential upward pressure on global yields; directly relevant to rates and market positioning.

Rates.title: Emerging Asia Bonds Draw Global Funds Despite Fed Hike Fears
Rates.reason: Flows into Emerging Asia bond markets despite Fed hike fears suggest continued external demand for higher-yield bonds (supportive for EM bond prices). Positive for EM rates but lower relevance to core global rates.

FX.title: Japanese Yen: Higher Japanese rates and intervention risks – MUFG
FX.summary: MUFG strategist Michael Wan argues Japanese rates "clearly have to head higher" after a positive Tankan survey, strong capital investment appetite and rising inflation expectations.
FX.reason: Higher Japanese rates and explicit intervention risk point to a durable JPY-supportive regime (JPY strength → USD weakness). Central-bank/rates narrative raises relevance for FX flows and cross-market positioning.

FX.title: Japanese Yen receives support from stealth intervention risks
FX.summary: USD/JPY continues its downside after pulling back from 40-year highs, trading around 162.40 during the Asian hours on Thursday. The pair loses ground as the Japanese Yen (JPY) captures support from growing trader expectations of government intervention.
FX.reason: Intervention expectations are a direct USD/JPY flow driver; supports further JPY appreciation and raises FX market sensitivity to policy actions.

FX.title: Japan shifts to ambush intervention tactics against yen short sellers, sources say
FX.reason: Reuters report of a tactical shift in intervention is a high‑impact FX regime story — increases probability of episodic JPY strength and changes risk premia across USD/JPY and EM/JPY exposures.

FX.title: US Dollar Index Price Forecast: Weakens below 101.50, but keeps bullish tone ahead of NFP
FX.summary: The US Dollar Index (DXY), an index of the value of the US Dollar (USD) measured against a basket of six world currencies, currently trades near 101.20 in the early European trading hours on Thursday.
FX.reason: DXY moving below key level signals near-term USD weakness; DXY dynamics drive cross‑currency flows and risk appetite ahead of NFP — meaningful for FX market positioning.

FX.title: Euro: Downside risk toward key supports against US Dollar – UOB
FX.summary: United Overseas Bank’s (UOB) Quek Ser Leang highlights that EUR/USD closed softer at 1.1376 after choppy trading between 1.1361 and 1.1423. Short-term momentum is turning lower, with scope to test 1.1360 while keeping the major 1.1335 support intact.
FX.reason: Bank note flags EUR downside vs USD — a USD‑strength signal that directly influences DXY and major cross‑currency positioning.

FX.title: British Pound gathers strength to near 1.3300 on Burnham’s commitment to fiscal rules, NFP data loom
FX.summary: The GBP/USD pair gains traction to near 1.3290 during the Asian trading hours on Thursday. The British Pound (GBP) strengthens against the US Dollar (USD) as the UK's likely next Prime Minister, Andy Burnham, has eased market concerns by pledging strict fiscal
FX.reason: Domestic UK fiscal credibility story lifting GBP vs USD — relevant for GBP/USD flows and for DXY composition given GBP moves.

FX.title: Indonesian Rupiah pares losses as soft US data, Fed tone weigh on US Dollar
FX.summary: USD/IDR inches lower after opening at a bullish gap, remaining in the positive territory for the fourth consecutive day, trading around 18,030 during the Asian hours on Thursday.
FX.reason: Soft US data / Fed tone undermining USD has direct transmission to EMFX (USD/IDR lower). EM pair response signals broader USD sensitivity ahead of US data.

FX.title: Indian Rupee gains at open, supported by further decline in oil prices
FX.summary: The Indian Rupee (INR) opens higher against the US Dollar (USD) on Thursday after a sharp decline the previous day. The USD/INR pair declines to near 95.00 as lower oil prices due to progress in talks between the United States (US) and Iran have improved the a
FX.reason: Commodity-driven INR strength (lower oil) reduces USD/INR — a localized FX move with modest broader USD implications ahead of risk events.

Commodities.title: Silver Price Forecast: XAG/USD rises above $60.00 amid less hawkish Fed tone
Commodities.summary: XAG/USD gains ground for the third consecutive day, trading around $60.20 per troy ounce during the Asian hours on Thursday. Silver prices find support following a less hawkish tone than expected from Federal Reserve (Fed) Chairman Kevin Warsh at Wednesday's E
Commodities.reason: Less-hawkish Fed commentary lowers real rates and weakens USD, a clear positive driver for silver/precious metals; Fed signals are high-relevance macro flow for metals.

Commodities.title: Gold Holds Gain After Warsh Remarks Ease Fed Rate-Hike Prospects
Commodities.reason: Fed rhetoric reducing rate-hike odds is a major bullish macro impulse for gold via lower real rates and a softer USD; Bloomberg coverage signals market-significant transmission.

Commodities.title: WTI Oil dips below $68.00 amid news of progress in the US-Iran peace talks
Commodities.summary: Crude Oil prices extended their decline on Thursday, as Qatari mediators reported “positive progress” on the indirect talks between the US and Iran held in Doha on Tuesday.
Commodities.reason: Progress on US‑Iran talks reduces geopolitical risk premium for Middle East barrels, producing a meaningful near-term downward impulse for oil prices.

Commodities.title: Oil prices on pace for fourth straight weekly loss as Trump sees progress in U.S.-Iran talks
Commodities.summary: Oil prices fell more than 1% on Wednesday after talks between Washington and Tehran concluded.
Commodities.reason: Confirmation of multi-day losses tied to eased US‑Iran tensions — reinforces the dominant short-term narrative of a lower oil risk premium and price softening.

Commodities.title: U.S. commercial crude oil inventories have decreased in June
Commodities.summary: For the week ending June 19, 2026, U.S. refineries processed 17.1 million barrels per day (b/d) of crude oil, down 81,000 b/d from the previous week, and they operated at 96.1% capacity utilization. Gasoline production averaged 9.5 million b/d, and distillate
Commodities.reason: Official EIA data showing a drawdown in U.S. commercial crude inventories is a supportive fundamental for oil prices and offsets some of the geo‑political-driven weakness.

Commodities.title: China’s Private Refiners Snap Up Middle East Oil as Prices Slide
Commodities.reason: Chinese buying of discounted Middle East barrels reflects demand response to lower prices — a supportive flow for crude that partially counters near-term risk‑premium declines.

Commodities.title: Oil: Hormuz risks and US-Iran MoU tensions – Rabobank
Commodities.summary: Rabobank strategist Michael Every describes how US efforts to secure Hormuz Oil flows under an emerging US-Iran MoU were reportedly blocked by Saudi Arabia, raising regional security risks.
Commodities.reason: Analysis highlighting heightened Strait of Hormuz/regional risks is a direct upside force for oil prices; serves as a countervailing risk to the peace‑talks-driven softening.

Commodities.title: U.S. refining capacity decreased during 2025
Commodities.summary: U.S. operable atmospheric distillation capacity, the primary measure of refinery capacity, totaled 18.2 million barrels per calendar day (b/cd) on January 1, 2026-down over 250,000 b/cd (about 1%) compared with January 1, 2025-according to our latest annual Re
Commodities.reason: A reduction in U.S. refining capacity is a structural supportive factor for crude and product markets (tighter processing capacity), though the signal is more medium-term than immediate.

Commodities.title: Oil Extends Decline as Barrels Flow Through Strait of Hormuz
Commodities.reason: Reporting that oil has fallen as flows through the Strait of Hormuz normalize reinforces the short-term downward pressure from reduced geopolitical risk premiums.

Crypto.title: Citi slashes 12-month bitcoin, ether targets as ETF flows dry up
Crypto.reason: ETF inflows were a dominant liquidity driver for BTC/ETH earlier in the year; Citi cutting targets and noting ETF flow fatigue is a clear bearish signal for crypto risk assets and near-term price support.

Crypto.title: Bitcoin opens the third quarter in an historical red zone after rare losing first half
Crypto.reason: Macro/seasonal framing that BTC has started the quarter weak reinforces negative momentum and risk sentiment for crypto in the near term.

Crypto.title: Bitcoin's long-term holders have returned to accumulation
Crypto.reason: On-chain accumulation by long-term holders is a constructive supply-side signal that can underpin BTC prices and suggests stronger investor conviction after recent weakness.

Crypto.title: Ark Invest bought more than $75 million of crypto shares during June bloodbath
Crypto.reason: Significant institutional buy-the-dip flows from a high-profile manager point to demand coming into distressed levels, supporting a recovery narrative for crypto risk assets.

Crypto.title: Cantor says bitcoin bear market may be entering final stretch
Crypto.reason: Analyst view signalling the bear market nearing its end reinforces a transition narrative from capitulation to early recovery, lifting sentiment across crypto markets.

Crypto.title: Ethereum Foundation lays out use cases for governments, institutions in new policy guide
Crypto.reason: Policy guidance aimed at governments and institutions is a direct institutional-adoption signal for Ethereum, supporting medium-term fundamental demand for ETH and ecosystem services.

Crypto.title: Ethereum Institutional launch draws support from across the Ethereum ecosystem
Crypto.reason: An explicit institutional-focused product/launch with ecosystem backing materially increases potential institutional flows into ETH and related infrastructure, a constructive structural tailwind.

Crypto.title: Ethereum gets a new nonprofit focused on institutional adoption
Crypto.reason: Additional organized institutional outreach bolsters the adoption narrative for Ethereum, though this is more supportive/structural than an immediate liquidity shock.

Crypto.title: Robinhood rolls out public blockchain as it expands deeper into crypto
Crypto.reason: Major retail broker expanding into blockchain infrastructure suggests broader retail distribution and product innovation, supporting crypto adoption and long-term demand.

Crypto.title: XRP, HYPE funds are the bright spots as investors flee bitcoin, ether ETFs
Crypto.reason: Flow rotation into niche alt funds indicates some intra-crypto redistribution; marginally positive for alt segments but underscores weakening ETF demand for BTC/ETH.

Crypto.title: Ether, solana, dogecoin in the green after Warsh comments push bitcoin above $60,000
Crypto.reason: Short-term macro commentary (Warsh) lifting BTC and correlated altcoins is a positive intraday liquidity/sentiment move but lower relevance for structural trends.
